result.one_liner: Project management and work tracking platform with REST API, OAuth/token authentication, and official MCP server support.

evidence.quote: API keys (the older method of authenticating) are being shut off, and Personal Access Tokens (PATs) are the direct replacement for API keys.
OAuth 2.0 provides delegated access to Asana resources with user-facing authorization flows.
You can generate a personal access token from the Asana developer console.
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON or form-encoded requests, returns JSON, and uses standard HTTP features.
Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, accessible via app integration, which allows AI assistants and other applications to access the Asana Work Graph.
Comprehensive reference for objects, schemas, and endpoints with in-context API explorer.

result.notes: Asana uses Personal Access Tokens (bearer_token auth) as the modern authentication method, with OAuth2 for delegated access. API breadth estimated as medium based on documented comprehensive endpoint coverage; exact endpoint count not publicly stated. Official MCP server (V2) now generally available for AI agent integration. Self-serve credentials available from developer console—no admin approval or payment required for basic API access.
